findings.detail: Actual 7.0.14 pidfd_poll delays an exited thread-group leader while siblings survive. Retaining PIDFD_THREAD alone was insufficient. The reviewed source also opens the live creator's read-only /proc/thread-self/stat before clone, verifies procfs/TID, and reads that same held FD after both initial PDEATHSIG arming and credential rearming.

Closing the held stat before MAPPED left CLONE_PARENT PID1 arming with the same pidfd-only blind spot. The reviewed source retains stat FD 5 through MAPPED and clone; nested arming checks the same stat and PIDFD, then closes 4/5 before mount/TreeReady. Keeper closes 4/5 after handoff. Actual nested leader and PID1/empty-base qualification has not run.

A helper panic after main-leader SYS_exit(0) could otherwise leave a successful process status. Helper bodies now use catch_unwind and explicit nonzero process exit on failure; the outer initial/rearm runner also requires exactly one true exit125/reaped record.

code_review.fd_mapping: All three sources duplicated with F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC minimum 6 before clone; child has private FD table and remaps to 3/4/5 before close_range(6..).
code_review.identity: The held proc inode retains the exact struct pid; raw children never reopen numeric TID paths. Kernel pread offset zero refreshes seq_file rather than reusing prevalidation output.
code_review.parser: Fixed 4096-byte pread, count>0 and count<4096, final newline, exact TID, final comm closing parenthesis, known live task state, field9 flags with checked decimal parsing; Z/X/PF_EXITING, missing/malformed/truncated data or read failure reject.
code_review.fd_lifecycle: CREATED and MAPPED retain only 3/4/5. ParkOnly after Enter retains 3/4. Nested init and keeper after tree handoff retain only 3.
code_review.scope: Normal public admission and frozen r5 private-dev implementation are not widened by this two-file change.
